title: Tech execs are spending less time managing and more time coding
excerpt: Some tech leaders are returning to coding, balancing management with time doing hands-on software development.
content_html:
Jean-Michel Lemieux missed building things with people.

The former chief technology officer at Shopify served on boards and dabbled in VC work, yet said that leadership alone left him too far removed from the work.

"I'm in these board meetings, and it feels like I'm a coach of a pro team, but I can't see them play the game," Lemieux, 54, said.

He said he loves the energy of "hands on keyboard." So, these days, he's working at Spellbook, which makes an AI copilot for lawyers. With the title "executive individual contributor," he's able to both lead and build.

"I love that adrenaline," he said.

For Lemieux and executives like him, going back to software development isn't only about revisiting an old passion. AI is transforming software development so quickly that some tech leaders are choosing to spend less time managing and more time building.

Back in the trenches

Reza Khadjavi feels the same urgency to build as the CEO of Motion, which created an "AI coworker" for marketers.

A couple of years ago, he began spending more time trying to understand AI and became "really fired up" because he said once-in-a-generation technological changes create enormous opportunities. At the same time, Khadjavi was also terrified, thinking, "If I don't go into the weeds on this stuff, the company might die."

So, while he hadn't written a line of code in about a decade, Khadjavi bought a Mac mini and loaded it with an AI agent to help him research various tasks.

Eventually, Khadjavi shared the agent with others at his Toronto company, which has about 80 people. "It just started taking off internally," he said, as staffers began asking the agent questions for their own work.

The experience "really changed my perspective of what it means to be a leader at a technology company," Khadjavi said. He said it became clear that the conventional wisdom that leaders had to delegate and focus on setting a vision was becoming outmoded. That meant that at times, Khadjavi could act more like an individual contributor.

Working on the AI agent allowed him to feel like, ''OK, I spent some time, I built something, and that thing is useful to the rest of the team."

Staying close to the work

After leaving his role as an engineering manager at Meta in May, Robert Sweeney looked for jobs in and out of leadership, on the condition that any management roles would allow him to spend at least 30% of his time building software.

Sweeney landed at Citizen Health, a healthtech company that helps patients with rare diseases share their medical records to accelerate research. Sweeney now spends half his time managing and half building software.

Working alongside engineers has convinced him that leaders need to stay close to the quickly evolving work.

"I felt like I couldn't be a pure manager anymore, even if I wanted to, because I couldn't understand the work that they were doing," he said.

"How can a director or a senior manager even hold the engineering team accountable at all if he has no concept of what it takes to build the software?" Sweeney said.

The risk of getting too hands-on

Not every executive thinks getting back to building is the right move. Sameer Ranjan, chief technology officer at the Dallas AI startup Catenate, said he still enjoys tinkering with software, but believes his time is better spent guiding the firm's direction than cranking out code.

"I left that chair so that somebody else can come and sit there," he said.

One risk for execs who do rank-and-file work is getting so caught up in the details that they lose sight of the broader business. That's something that Lemieux, at Spellbook, said he's guarding against.

"The failure mode of this role is: I end up doing everything," he said. To prevent that, Lemieux said he limits where he gets involved by looking for "the big boulder that I've got to move," and when he does drop into a project, he lets the team know he might only be involved for a couple of months.

Lemieux views his job as temporary help on a project, a bit like a Navy SEAL: "Coming in, landing, making sure things are in a good spot."

His role, he said, is to improve the team by working with them to improve the product. This way, when Lemieux moves to another area of the company, the team is left with tools or approaches they can continue to use, he said.

Lemieux said he arrives on a project ready to learn and makes clear that he's not an auditor. "I'm not here to just whisper to the CEO all the time and tell him everything that's going on," Lemieux said. "There's a big trust factor here."

He said he tries to show up humbly. That might mean fixing bugs or writing the first draft of a press release. "I'm not just there to tell them what to do, but I'm there to do it with them," Lemieux said.

He also reads the code and project docs to get up to speed. "I can't come in as a pointy-headed manager," Lemieux said. "I'll do the homework to understand things deeply enough that I'm not a burden on the team."

Ultimately, he said, working this way is appealing in part because, beyond being a VC or a board member, there is no widely known career path for builders like himself.

Lemieux said his goal is to help the staffers he works with grow faster and do more than they think they can. He believes working alongside them as an individual contributor — not solely managing them — makes that possible.

"Our bet is the company could be five times better than it would be without doing this," Lemieux said.

content_html_zh:
让-米歇尔·勒米厄 (Jean-Michel Lemieux) 怀念与人一起创造事物的时光。

这位 Shopify 前首席技术官曾在董事会任职，并涉足风险投资工作，但他表示，仅凭领导力就让他远离了工作。

“我参加这些董事会会议，感觉就像我是一支职业球队的教练，但我看不到他们玩游戏，”54 岁的勒米厄说。

他说他喜欢“双手放在键盘上”的能量。 所以，现在他在 Spellbook 工作，该公司为律师提供人工智能副驾驶。 凭借“执行个人贡献者”的头衔，他能够同时领导和建设。

“我喜欢那种肾上腺素，”他说。

对于 Lemieux 和像他这样的高管来说，重返软件开发不仅仅是重温旧日的热情。 人工智能正在如此迅速地改变软件开发，以至于一些技术领导者选择花更少的时间进行管理，而花更多的时间进行构建。

回到战壕

Reza Khadjavi 与 Motion 的首席执行官一样感受到了建设的紧迫性，该公司为营销人员创建了“人工智能同事”。

几年前，他开始花更多时间尝试理解人工智能，并变得“真正兴奋”，因为他说千载难逢的技术变革创造了巨大的机会。 与此同时，卡贾维也感到害怕，心想：“如果我不深入研究这件事，公司可能就会灭亡。”

因此，虽然 Khadjavi 大约有十年没有写过一行代码，但他还是买了一台 Mac mini，并在其中加载了人工智能代理来帮助他研究各种任务。

最终，Khadjavi 与他位于多伦多的公司（该公司约有 80 名员工）的其他人共享了该代理。 “这在内部才刚刚开始，”他说，同时工作人员开始就自己的工作向特工询问问题。

卡贾维说，这次经历“确实改变了我对成为科技公司领导者意味着什么的看法”。 他表示，很明显，领导者必须授权并专注于制定愿景的传统智慧已经过时。 这意味着有时，卡贾维可以表现得更像个人贡献者。

开发人工智能代理让他感觉，“好吧，我花了一些时间，我构建了一些东西，而那东西对团队的其他成员很有用。”

贴近工作

罗伯特·斯威尼 (Robert Sweeney) 5 月份辞去 Meta 的工程经理一职后，开始在领导层内外寻找工作，条件是任何管理职位都允许他花至少 30% 的时间构建软件。

斯威尼加入了 Citizen Health，这是一家医疗科技公司，帮助罕见疾病患者分享他们的医疗记录以加速研究。 斯威尼现在一半的时间用于管理，一半的时间用于构建软件。

与工程师一起工作使他确信领导者需要密切关注快速发展的工作。

“我觉得我不能再成为一名纯粹的经理，即使我愿意，因为我无法理解他们正在做的工作，”他说。

“如果董事或高级经理不知道如何构建软件，他怎么能让工程团队承担责任呢？” 斯威尼说道。

过于亲力亲为的风险

并非所有高管都认为重返建设是正确的举措。 达拉斯人工智能初创公司 Catenate 的首席技术官 Sameer Ranjan 表示，他仍然喜欢修补软件，但相信他的时间最好花在指导公司的方向上，而不是编写代码。

“我离开了那把椅子，以便其他人可以过来坐在那里，”他说。

对于从事普通工作的高管来说，面临的一个风险是过于关注细节，而忽视了更广泛的业务。 Spellbook 的 Lemieux 表示他正在防范这种情况。

“这个角色的失败模式是：我最终做了所有事情，”他说。 为了防止这种情况发生，勒米厄表示，他通过寻找“我必须搬动的大石头”来限制自己参与的范围，当他确实投入到一个项目时，他会让团队知道他可能只会参与几个月。

勒米厄将他的工作视为项目的临时帮助，有点像海豹突击队：“进来，着陆，确保一切都在一个好的位置。”

他说，他的职责是通过与团队合作改进产品来改进团队。 他说，这样，当 Lemieux 调到公司的另一个领域时，团队就可以保留可以继续使用的工具或方法。

勒米厄表示，他刚开始一个项目时就已经做好了学习的准备，并明确表示自己不是审计员。 勒米厄说：“我来这里不是为了一直对首席执行官耳语并告诉他发生的一切。” “这里有一个很大的信任因素。”

他说他试图表现得谦虚。 这可能意味着修复错误或撰写新闻稿的初稿。 “我不仅在那里告诉他们该做什么，而且我在那里和他们一起做，”勒米厄说。

他还阅读代码和项目文档以加快速度。 “我不能以一个尖锐的经理的身份出现，”勒米厄说。 “我会做功课，深入理解事情，这样我就不会成为团队的负担。”

他说，最终，这种工作方式很有吸引力，部分原因是，除了成为风险投资家或董事会成员之外，像他这样的建设者没有广为人知的职业道路。

勒米厄表示，他的目标是帮助与他一起工作的员工更快成长，并做得比他们想象的更多。 他相信，作为个人贡献者与他们一起工作——而不仅仅是管理他们——使这成为可能。

勒米厄说：“我们打赌，如果不这样做，公司的业绩可能会好五倍。”
